messages:
olga: Heads-up — around 09:10 we had a burst of spot GPU interruptions in us-west-2. ~12 pods got stuck waiting, cluster-autoscaler didn't kick over to on-demand fast enough. Some jobs hit OOM/CrashLoopBackoff :grimacing:

samir: Any autoscaler logs? which nodegroups are involved?

maya: It looks like two spot ASGs and one on-demand warm pool. ASG sizes: spot-gpu: 0-200, od-warm: 1-4. Autoscaler flags were standard.

kevin: infra-bot posted the interruption events earlier:

infra-bot: AWS Spot interruption notice: instance i-0abcd1234efg, termination-time: 2024-07-26T09:11:30Z

jessie: Root cause seems to be scale-up ordering + taint use. We taint spot nodes with node.k8s.capacity=spot:NoSchedule and only batch workloads tolerate it. But some longer-lived jobs without toleration landed on spot because we recently changed nodeSelector.

olga: So two problems: 1) critical jobs landed on spot because tolerations missing, 2) autoscaler delayed creating on-demand nodes to replace capacity because of scale-up grooming/backpressure.

samir: Quick mitigation: add a cheap failover toleration/affinity for our controller manager so it will prefer on-demand, and lower cluster-autoscaler scale-up delay for nodegroup od-warm to 20s during incidents. Can we change that safely?

maya: Patch proposal: annotate critical workloads with "cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: 'false'" and enforce podPriority > 100000 for control-plane-ish things. Also restore explicit nodeGroup weights:

```yaml
# autoscaler flags snippet
--nodes=1:4:od-warm
--nodes=0:200:spot-gpu
--max-node-provision-time=5m
--expander=priority
```

kevin: Another idea: make on-demand warm pool hold 1 GPU per AZ instead of single zone to reduce cross-AZ provisioning time. Also add a preemption handler to accelerate eviction and drain so we don't rely on full autoscaler response.

jessie: For interruption handling we should use the instance metadata/IMDS hook + tombstone annotation pattern, plus a short-lived local cache to avoid double-draining. Current termination-handler timeout is 120s; suggest 30s to speed failover.

olga: Cost tradeoff note: keeping 3x small on-demand nodes across zones will add ~6-8% baseline cost, but should cut user-visible GPU-serving tail latency from 800ms to ~150ms during spot churn. Worth it for prod tier.

samir: Action items:
- maya -> create a small PR to enforce tolerations/affinity for critical workloads (KEPT ON-DEMAND)
- kevin -> coord with infra to change od-warm to 3 per AZ and adjust autoscaler flags (canary on dev first)
- jessie -> reduce termination-handler timeout to 30s and add local tombstone dedupe
- olga -> run a cost runbook to quantify incremental spend and SLA improvement

maya: I'll open PR and tag @kevin and @olga.

kevin: If we do this, let's also add a quick chaos test (single-AZ spot drain) to validate warm pool + autoscaler order. Schedule it low-risk (weekend canary). :hammer:

olga: Agreed. If we pass the canary we keep the config. If not, rollback. Thanks team :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Created issue #INFRA-4278: "heterogeneous warm-pool + autoscaler ordering canary" and linked this thread.
